sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Broad Jump is an explosive lower body plyometric exercise that develops horizontal power.

The athlete loads into a quarter squat, swings the arms back, then explodes forward to cover as much horizontal distance as possible before landing softly on both feet.

It is a foundational athletic test and training tool for sprinting, jumping, and field sport performance.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Develops horizontal explosive power
- Trains triple extension of the hips, knees, and ankles
- Improves sprint acceleration mechanics
- Builds reactive strength and elasticity
- Reinforces soft, balanced landings
- Highly transferable to field and court sports
- Requires no equipment beyond open space

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Quadriceps, Gluteus Maximus, Hamstrings

Secondary: Calves, Hip Flexors, Core, Shoulders

sections.heading: Set Up
sections.content:
1. Find a flat, non-slip surface with several metres of clear space ahead.
2. Mark a starting line on the ground.
3. Wear supportive athletic footwear.

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart at the starting line.
2. Keep your knees slightly bent and ready to jump forward.
3. Brace your core and look forward.

sections.heading: Load and Launch
sections.content:
1. Lower into a quarter squat position.
2. Swing your arms backward to generate momentum.
3. Explode forward, swinging your arms forward as you jump as far as you can, pushing off with both feet.

sections.heading: Land and Reset
sections.content:
1. Land softly on both feet with your knees bent to absorb the impact.
2. Stabilise your landing before standing up.
3. Walk back to the starting line and reset for the next rep.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Landing with stiff legs and no knee bend
- Letting the knees collapse inward on landing
- Failing to use the arm swing for momentum
- Landing on the heels instead of the full foot
- Performing reps when fatigued, leading to poor mechanics
- Jumping vertically instead of horizontally
- Skipping the warm-up before plyometrics

sections.heading: Equipment Required
sections.content:
- Flat, non-slip training surface
- Optional measuring tape or distance markers
- Supportive athletic footwear

sections.heading: Body Position
sections.content:
1. Feet shoulder-width apart at the line.
2. Knees soft, hips loaded.
3. Arms ready to drive through the jump.

sections.heading: Movement Setup
sections.content:
1. Quarter squat depth on the load.
2. Powerful triple extension on take-off.
3. Soft two-foot landing with the feet underneath the hips.

sections.heading: Safety Considerations
sections.content:
- Always warm up the lower body before plyometrics
- Stop the session if landings become sloppy
- Avoid wet or slippery surfaces
- Limit volume to maintain quality of each rep
- Stop immediately if you feel sharp knee or ankle pain
